title: You're Taller in the Morning
sources: Adults lose roughly 1 cm (often 1-2 cm) of standing height over the course of a day, mostly within the first hours after getting up (Tyrrell, Reilly & Troup 1985, Spine; Reilly et al. 1984)
The loss comes from the intervertebral discs: compressive load during upright activity squeezes fluid out of the discs, so they get thinner (Adams et al. 1987; McGill 1996)
Lying down unloads the spine and the discs re-absorb fluid overnight, restoring height by morning (Tyrrell et al. 1985)
Astronauts can grow up to 3% taller in microgravity as the spine lengthens (NASA, 'Bigger in Space'; Young & Rajulu 2011 NASA study)
After returning to Earth, astronauts return to their normal height within months (NASA)
